To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) enterocyte autoantigen‐dependent cellular cytotoxicty is the prevalent mechanism of enterocyte apoptosis in patients with autoimmune enteropathies but not in coelic patients; (2) the Fas/FasL and perforin pathways do not seem to be involved in enterocyte apoptosis in these conditions; and (3) the Fas‐mediated pathway seems to be the predominant mechanism of enterocyte cell death in patients with coelic disease.

(i) the mechanisms of villous atrophies are different in autoimmune enteropathy from that in coeliac disease; (ii) in autoimmune enteropathy, enterocyte autoantigens are targeted by autoantibodies that trigger apoptosis of enterocytes; (iii) in coeliac disease enterocyte apoptosis is triggered by Fas ligand‐mediated signalling, and perforin cytotoxic granules, and not by autoantibody.

(i) enterocyte apoptosis is a prominent feature of autoimmune enteropathy and of coeliac disease; (ii) in autoimmune enteropathy the increased enterocyte apoptosis is mediated by autoantibodies through antibody‐dependent cellular toxicity, whereas in coeliac disease it is triggered by cytotoxic T cells; and (iii) Fas/FasL and perforin cytotoxic granules do not play a role in the pathogenesis of villous atrophic lesions of autoimmune enteropathy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms of villous atrophic changes in coeliac disease and in autoimmune enteropathy, a rare disorder with similar clinical manifestations.

the mechanisms of villous atrophia in autoimmune enteropathy (AE), which is a rare disorder characterized by severe malabsorption, chronic diarrhoea, weight loss and villous atrophy, in the absence of any identifiable aetiological factor.
the study of mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of coeliac disease and autoimmune enteropathy, two conditions sharing a number of features.
